value.body: Handles the everyday people work in an organisation — scheduling interviews, onboarding new joiners, maintaining employee records, attendance and leave, and explaining policies. HR executives work in companies of every size, staffing and recruitment agencies, and shared-services centres. A typical day involves coordinating with candidates and managers, updating HR systems and answering employee queries.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: BBA (HR), BA (Psychology or Sociology) or B.Com
items.note: An MBA/PGDM in HR is common for larger corporate HR teams

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Excel, HR management software, job portals

items.label: Laws you meet
items.value: Labour codes, PF and ESI rules, state Shops & Establishments Acts

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers commonly start as HR trainees, recruiters or HR executives in a staffing firm or a company HR team. Internships, clear communication and Excel skills help; an MBA or PGDM in HR is the usual route into larger corporate HR teams. Recruitment-heavy roles are often the most accessible first step.

value.title: At a glance
items: Growth path: HR executive → HR generalist or business partner → HR manager, or a specialism such as talent acquisition, payroll or learning & development.
Much early work is administrative, and recruitment roles are often target-driven.
Confidentiality and judgement about people matter as much as process knowledge.
